subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron/heartbeat authority be implemented as a narrow per-job/heartbeat marker now, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent trust boundary determines where elevated authority is created, stored, audited, migrated, and revalidated for host exec.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader schedule-authority model so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one non-forgeable authority contract.

options.title: Implement narrow elevated markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with explicit migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Remove internal-source elevation
options.body: Fail closed for cron-event and heartbeat elevated access unless maintainers intentionally preserve a separate compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader schedule-authority model so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one non-forgeable authority contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently owned the adjacent Gateway cron caller identity implementation and proof path that this authority model would extend.
